In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the innate psychological needs identified by SDT are the most comprehensive and are the most widely studied and accepted.
social media use can satisfy a range of innate and learned needs and motivations.
the innate psychological needs of social media use are: (1) competence (i.e., feeling of efficacy), (2) autonomy (i.e., freedom), (3) self-actualization, and (4) ownership.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the innate psychological needs of autonomy, competence, and relatedness (SDT) are closely aligned with the need for self-determination (POT), and that these needs are also closely aligned with Maslow’s (and Alderfer’s) psychological needs for self-actualization, esteem, and love/belonging.

the needs identified in these perspectives can be classified into two broad categories of needs: needs for relatedness (e.g., belongingness, affiliation, love, and acceptance) and needs for competence (e.g., autonomy, competence, and control).
the needs identified by SDT (autonomy, competence, and relatedness) map to the needs for self-determination, self-efficacy, and social connection identified by POT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these two theories complement each other.
